lines.text: Let's set up ClipForge, from download to your first video.
Start on Home. Scroll down to Render agent and download it. The agent renders your videos on your own PC, using your own connection.
Unzip it into its own folder. Inside is ffmpeg, the engine that cuts your clips, adds the banner and captions, and encodes the video. Keep it with the agent.
Now run ClipForgeAgent. Your browser opens with a code. Check it matches the one in the agent's window, click Pair it, and that's done.
Next, Settings. Say what your niche is, and add a few search terms.
Lines one and two are the banner across the top of every video.
Then the part that matters most. Paste a playlist, or name the YouTube channels to take clips from. That's how you get the clips you actually want.
Full-length videos are fine in a playlist. The AI finds the best moments and cuts them in for you.
Turn on Only from one show to keep every clip on your niche, then save.
Back on Home, connect your YouTube channel. Set up publishing walks you through it.
When everything says Ready, click Publish now.
That's it. ClipForge takes it from here.
